title: COVID Brain Fog May Not Be Irreversible - Nautilus
gist: A Neuroprotection study following more than 2,000 Omicron-wave COVID patients in China found that cognitive decline from the Omicron variant was not irreversible for everyone—two-thirds showed no decline and 22% recovered over two years.

insights.claim: The original SARS-CoV-2 virus and the Alpha and Delta variants were particularly damaging to cognition, while the Omicron variant proved milder.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Distinguishes cognitive risk by variant, relevant to interpreting long-COVID 'brain fog' outcomes.
insights.locator: proved to be particularly cruel in that regard, but the Omicron variant was a little milder

insights.claim: A Neuroprotection study followed more than 2,000 patients hospitalized during China's Omicron wave (December 2022 to March 2023), testing cognition at six months and two years after discharge.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Establishes the longitudinal design behind the reversibility finding.
insights.locator: followed more than 2,000 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 during the Omicron wave

insights.claim: Two-thirds of the patients showed no cognitive decline at all, and nearly a quarter (22%) experienced reversible cognitive decline, with scores rising an average of three points out of 40.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Provides encouraging evidence that Omicron-related brain fog can improve over time in many patients.
insights.locator: Two-third of the patients showed no decline in their mental faculties at all
